A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PGM research by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained methods and experiments can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original language-model training, text generation, distillation, downstream evaluation and ImageNet experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original language-model results and reports revised image experiments, expanded downstream and distillation evaluations, and longer-context timing results.

M1.justification: The partition loss, encoder–GroupSwap–decoder architecture, query initialization options and Algorithms 1–4 are retained. V2 adds class conditioning and classifier-free guidance for image generation, plus optional nucleus sampling with p=0.9 for distilled text models. These extend conditioning and inference without substantially redesigning PGM.

E1.justification: ImageNet was already evaluated in v1, but v2 replaces unconditional generation with a class-conditional task. V2 also adds BoolQ, OpenBookQA, RACE and SIQA in Table 2 while retaining the earlier seven-task evaluation in Table 4. LM1B and OpenWebText remain covered.

E2.justification: The image comparison replaces MDLM with MaskGIT, an image-specific comparator, in v2 Tables 8–9. Distilled MDLM also enters downstream comparisons; v1 evaluated MDLM+SDTT only for generation. The ordinary MDLM, complementary-masking MDLM and GPT-2 language comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The image protocol changes from 256 to 1024 image tokens, 12 to 24 transformer blocks, 1M to 500k training steps, and 10k to 50k evaluation images, alongside revised optimizer and batch settings. V2 introduces confidence/Halton sampling with guidance sweeps. Its distillation study uses five-round BF16/FP32 comparisons instead of v1's five/seven-round FP32/FP64 grid, and adds nucleus decoding, downstream evaluation after distillation and 4096-token timing.

E4.justification: V2 adds image guidance-strength, sampler and encoder/decoder-allocation comparisons; nucleus-sampling quality/diversity/speed analysis; downstream accuracy before and after distillation; and longer-context efficiency analysis. The earlier seven-round and FP64 distillation comparisons disappear. Complementary-masking, query-initialization and training-stability analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The 100-batch training and 20-batch text timing protocols with standard deviations remain. V2's image tables instead report averages over ten batches without standard deviations, whereas v1's image timings included them. Removing the checklist also removes v1's explicit statement that training was not repeated across seeds; v2 does not establish additional seeded training runs.

E6.justification: Image and distillation result sets are substantially replaced or expanded under revised protocols, and downstream and 4096-token timing results are added. V2 Table 9 reports best-guidance 32-step FID/throughput of 5.54/7.93 images/s for PGM 12/12 versus 5.35/1.05 for MaskGIT; these are not same-setting improvements over v1. The reported OWT PGM 8/8 validation perplexity changes from 22.70 to 22.61. Undistilled OWT generation results and Table 4's downstream scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds formal definitions for MaskGIT confidence and classifier-free guided log probabilities in Sections 2.4–2.5, and states exact rather than approximate diffusion endpoint conditions. The PGM loss, GroupSwap equations and conditional-likelihood argument remain unchanged. The earlier NELBO integral is restated through the weighted cross-entropy objective; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes text generation and describes image results as preliminary. V2 makes image efficiency a central abstract, introduction and conclusion claim: approximately 7.5-fold throughput at comparable FID, or better FID with twice the steps while retaining a speed advantage. V1's headline 10.73-fold acceleration over cached GPT-2 after distillation is removed, while general distillation compatibility remains claimed.

C2.justification: V2 interprets nucleus sampling as narrowing the distilled PGM quality/diversity gap while reducing its speed advantage. Appendix A newly attributes parameter inefficiency to GroupSwap and proposes exploiting block-diagonal attention. Appendix D.6 explicitly limits the 4096-token evidence to timing without training at that length. The preliminary-image qualification disappears, while training overhead and unresolved multimodal applicability remain.

D1.justification: V2 substantially revises image implementation and hyperparameter documentation, including the HaltonMaskGIT codebase, cropping, conditioning, registers and guidance. It newly specifies the OWT holdout/document separator and model parameter counts. Conversely, v1's distillation steps-per-round disclosure, image training-cost rows and checklist statements about an attached code ZIP and scripts disappear. Both retain a future MIT-release promise; actual external availability cannot be established from these PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds substantial positioning against Esoteric Language Models in Appendix B, contrasting objectives, supervision, attention and caching. Section 6 expands discussion of flexible-length diffusion, stochastic interpolants and edit flows. This shifts the related-work emphasis from v1's detailed distillation and other-modality discussion toward hybrid and variable-length models, beyond citation-format or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background and method exposition are extensively rewritten. The separate motivation/approach subsections are consolidated, six experimental subsections become three broader sections, limitations move to an appendix, acknowledgements are added, and the NeurIPS checklist is removed. These constitute substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a combined image/text throughput display instead of a small text-latency plot, and Figure 3 is redrawn. The distillation plot is redesigned and moved into the main text. A parameter/perplexity/efficiency summary replaces the main ablation table, which moves to the appendix. Downstream and distillation tables are restructured, and new guidance-sweep and longer-context tables substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evidence for practical efficiency beyond text: v1's explicitly preliminary image study becomes a nearly parameter-matched MaskGIT comparison with 50k-image evaluation and sampler/guidance controls. Downstream tests after distillation also strengthen the assessment of utility beyond generative perplexity. These gains outweigh localized reporting weaknesses, including inconsistent latency entries in Table 7 and lost reproducibility disclosures. The improvement rests on stronger comparisons and validation, not on treating the changed-setting image scores as direct gains over v1.
